title: Health & Wellness Ecommerce Benchmarks for 2026
summary: Conversion rate, average order value, and bounce rate benchmarks in the Health and Wellness category in Ecommerce for 2026.
body_markdown:
## Still the Highest-Converting Category but Bounce Rates Are Climbing


The benchmarks from January to September 2026:[3.22% median CVR](https://getshogun.com/benchmarks/ecommerce-conversion-rate) ,[$174 median AOV](https://getshogun.com/benchmarks/ecommerce-average-order-value) . Health & Wellness ranks first in conversion rate across the 10 published industries — the only category in the dataset above 3.2 and 1.48 points above the cross-industry median of 1.74%.


Source: Shogun 2026 Year-to-Date Ecommerce Benchmark Reports (January–September 2026), Health & Wellness.


CVR rose 3.7% from Q2 to Q3 among stores active in both quarters — a gain, but smaller than the category’s usual summer lift. Over the same quarters in 2025, Health & Wellness grew 6.6%, so Q3 2026 came in 2.9 percentage points below that prior-year pattern. In context, it’s a solid result: across all stores, same-store CVR fell 4.5% from Q2 to Q3, and six of the ten published industries declined. Health & Wellness was one of only four that gained or held steady.


On order value: $174 is the lowest median in the dataset — Food & Beverage is also $174, a few cents higher. The P25-to-P75 range is $110–$320, a 2.9× spread and among the tightest of any category. Health & Wellness merchants tend to operate at consistent price points, with relatively little distance between top and bottom quartiles. AOV edged down from Q2 to Q3 (−1.2%, $181 to $179) among stores active in both quarters, tracking close to flat.


> Health & Wellness leads all 10 published categories in CVR at 3.22% — the highest median of any industry in the 2026 year-to-date dataset. It also posted a Q3 conversion gain in a quarter when most categories declined.


## **Conversion Rate Benchmark — 2026 Year to Date**


The median Health & Wellness CVR from January through September 2026 was 3.22%, first among the 10 published industries.


n=803 active Shopify stores, January–September 2026. Stores with CVR below 0.1% or above 25% excluded. Source: Shogun 2026 Year-to-Date CVR Benchmark Report.


The gap between Health & Wellness and the cross-industry median (1.74%) is the widest in the dataset — 1.57 percentage points. The P25 for Health & Wellness is 1.61% and the P75 is 5.94%, a 3.7× spread. At the top end, some stores in this category convert at rates typically seen in subscription or highly loyal DTC brands.


One pattern worth noting: the three top-converting categories — Health & Wellness, Beauty & Personal Care, and Food & Beverage — are also the three with the lowest median AOVs. The likely mechanism is repeat purchasing. Customers who know the product, trust the brand, and are restocking rather than evaluating for the first time tend to convert faster and in smaller dollar amounts per transaction. That’s a hypothesis the data supports but doesn’t prove.


> If your Health & Wellness store is converting below 3.22%, you’re below the category median. If you’re above 5.52%, you’re in the top quartile of a category that already leads the dataset.


## CVR & Bounce Rate Trend — January 2025 through September 2026


The graph below shows monthly median CVR and bounce rate for active Health & Wellness stores in Shogun’s conversion tracking network.


n=23–44 active stores per month. Each month measured on its own; CVR filter 0.1%–25% per site per month. Source: Shogun session and conversion tracking, Health & Wellness.


Two things stand out in the 21-month trend. The first is the late-2025 CVR surge: October through December 2025 all exceeded 4.5%, with December reaching 5.14% — well above every other month in the window. Whether that reflects year-end demand, a more engaged buyer mindset heading into the new year, or something specific to the stores in the cohort is unclear — but the signal is consistent across three consecutive months.


The second is bounce rate. Through 2025 it ran mostly between 50% and 55%. In 2026 it climbed steadily, passing 60% in April and reaching 61.5% in August and 62.6% in September — the highest readings in the 21-month window. CVR has held up despite the higher bounce rates, but this is now the clearest trend in the category’s data.


On a month-by-month year-over-year basis, every month of 2026 so far has run below its 2025 equivalent. The gap was widest in August (2.76% vs. 3.95%) and narrowest in September (3.72% vs. 3.75%), when conversion rebounded to essentially match the prior year. Q3 followed the same shape as the broader market: a solid July, a soft August and a September recovery.


## **Average Order Value Benchmark: 2026 Year to Date**


The 2026 year-to-date median AOV for Health & Wellness was $174. This data covers full-store Shopify order data, separate from the CVR cohort above.


January–September 2026, n=199 stores with at least 375 orders; AOV above $5,000 excluded. Source: Shogun 2026 Year-to-Date AOV Benchmark Report, Health & Wellness.


## AOV Trend: June 2025 through September 2026


The graph below tracks monthly median AOV for Health & Wellness stores, with each month measured on its own (176–194 stores per month).


n=176–194 stores per month; each month measured on its own (stores with at least 50 orders that month, AOV $1–$5,000). Source: Shogun AOV benchmark data, Health & Wellness.


The AOV trend remains one of the most tightly bounded in the dataset. With one exception, every month in the 16-month window sits between $166 and $183 — a $17 range. That is not volatility. Health & Wellness merchants appear to operate at highly stable price points, and that stability held through a period that saw meaningful movement in other categories.


The exception is November 2025 ($193). That’s also when CVR ran at 4.76%, part of the late-2025 surge. Both metrics peaked together. One possible explanation is that health and wellness products see increased purchasing around the holidays, as people stock up, gift supplements or wellness items, or make purchase decisions they’ve been putting off. But that’s a hypothesis, not a conclusion the data can confirm on its own.


Q3 2026 drifted down month by month — $178 in July, $173 in August and $170 in September — ending roughly level with September 2025 ($169). Across 2026, monthly AOV has run between $166 and $183, overlapping the mid-2025 range rather than sitting clearly above or below it.


On a matched same-store basis (n=148 stores active in both January–September 2025 and January–September 2026), median AOV moved from $180 to $173 — a −3.9% year-over-year change.


## **What CVR and AOV Are Saying Together**


Health & Wellness occupies an unusual position in the dataset. It has the highest CVR of any category. It also has the lowest median AOV and one of the tightest price-point distributions. That combination — frequent, confident purchasing at consistent, modest amounts — is the hallmark of a category built on repeat buying.


The Q2→Q3 CVR story is a relative win. At +3.7%, the gain ran 2.9 points below the category’s prior-year pattern (+6.6%), but it came in a quarter when same-store conversion across all stores fell 4.5%. Basket size is the softer side: AOV slipped 1.2% from Q2 to Q3 and is down 3.9% year over year among stores active in both periods.


Bounce rate is the area that most invites closer attention. Every Q3 month topped 60% at the median store, and August and September set new highs for the category. CVR has held up so far — likely because many of the visitors who stay are returning customers — but a sustained rise in bounce rates could eventually put pressure on conversion volume, especially as traffic costs rise.


> Health & Wellness is still the highest-converting category in the dataset, and it gained in a quarter when most categories slipped. The pressure points are elsewhere: basket sizes are down slightly year over year, and bounce rates are at their highest levels yet.


## **A Note on Sub-Markets Within Health & Wellness**


The P25-to-P75 spread of $110–$320 is among the tightest in the dataset at 2.9×. Most Health & Wellness merchants in this cohort operate within a relatively narrow AOV band. That said, the category covers a wide range of products — vitamins and supplements, personal care devices, fitness equipment, sleep aids, and more. The tight spread likely reflects that the bulk of this cohort sits in the consumables end of the market, where orders are smaller and more frequent.


Merchants in the medical devices or fitness equipment segments may see AOVs well above the P75 ($320) and CVRs below the category median — those sub-markets behave more like considered-purchase categories than repeat-purchase ones. If your store sells high-ticket wellness products, the $174 median AOV benchmark is probably the wrong reference point. The CVR benchmark is more universally applicable.


> At 3.22% median CVR with a P75 of 5.52%, Health & Wellness sets a high bar — and a higher one for stores that can replicate the repeat-purchase dynamics of the category’s top performers.
